# Q-Guard

> Q-Guard is a test automation tool by Q-Leap SA, a software testing company in
> Luxembourg. It observes how real users move through a web application, anonymises
> that data at the source, detects the journeys they repeat and turns them into test
> cases and Selenium scripts (Java, C#, Ruby, Python). It is installed on the
> customer's own servers under an annual licence that includes installation and support.

## Product

- [Home](https://q-guard.app/): what Q-Guard does and who it is for
- [How it works](https://q-guard.app/how-it-works/): from real usage to test cases and Selenium scripts
- [Features](https://q-guard.app/features/): test case generation, Selenium export, reports
- [Security & data](https://q-guard.app/security-and-data/): data flow, what is captured and stored, anonymisation at the source, on-premise storage, GDPR, deployment
- [Licence & trial](https://q-guard.app/licence-and-trial/): annual on-premise licence, installation, trial, support
- [FAQ](https://q-guard.app/support-help-faq/): licence, installation, data, trial
- [Q-Guard Test Runner](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/q-guard-test-runner/aefoifepleogeiicaclpdldfjppdpjbd): browser extension that runs Q-Guard test cases locally

## Security and data handling

- Deployment: on-premise only today, installed on the customer's own servers by the Q-Leap team; a hosted SaaS version is planned.
- Captured: sequences of user actions in the web application (sessions), in production or test environments.
- Anonymisation: the Q-Guard data collector drops every value users type before anything is stored; only the user journey is kept.
- Storage: user journeys, usage patterns, test cases, Selenium scripts and reports are stored on the customer's servers. No sensitive data is stored on Q-Leap's side.
- GDPR: designed with GDPR requirements in mind (data minimisation, anonymisation at the source, storage on customer infrastructure). It does not by itself make the customer's processing compliant.
- Installation: included in the annual licence, typically less than one day; a trial on the customer's own application is available.
